prediction_d_worse_at_small_n_and_high_d.evidence: square n=400/800/1600/3200 local D=1.4878/1.6530/1.6525/1.8439 and CONSTANT-metric D=1.4919/1.6811/1.6895/1.8035 -- identical trend, so it is not metric noise; in 3-D the LOCAL metric reads BETTER than the constant one (cube n=1600: 2.8170 vs 2.4252), the opposite of the prediction

actual_mechanism.name: fit-window depletion + survivorship conditioning, amplified by unweighted OLS
actual_mechanism.statement: gp_local_mahalanobis fits r in [0.01,0.5]*ref_scale where ref_scale is the median 20th-Mahalanobis-neighbour distance. A radius of f*r_20 holds ~20*f^d neighbours, so the ENTIRE window spans mean neighbour counts 0.009..4.5 per point at n=1600 -- at or below the point-spacing scale. At the bottom the total pair count is ~14 of 2.6M, and the `0 < C(r) < 1` filter conditions on 'at least one pair survived', flooring log C and flattening the curve.
actual_mechanism.smoking_gun: on the isotropic square the mean LOCAL slope over the lower half of the window is 1.168 and over the upper half is 1.976 -- the top of the window already reads the truth; unweighted OLS averages the truth with the artifact
actual_mechanism.why_the_global_arm_is_immune: it goes through baseline.correlation_dimension, whose window is [0.01,0.2]*bounding-box diagonal = mean neighbour counts ~1..400, two decades higher

fix.name: inverse-variance weighted log-log fit
fix.change: replace OLS on (log r, log C) with WLS using weights w_j = P_j, the observed pair count at radius j
fix.rationale: Var(log C_j) ~ 1/P_j to leading order and P_j spans 14..7.2e6 across this window, so OLS is the wrong error model; w_j = 1/Var is the standard correction
fix.zero_knob: introduces no constant, no threshold and no caller-facing parameter -- the weights ARE the data; the radius grid, reference scale, metric and distance arithmetic are unchanged
fix.scale_equivariance: rescaling the cloud rescales every radius and leaves every count identical, so the fit is exactly scale-equivariant -- the isotropic-control property is preserved by construction
fix.interaction_with_ridge_floors: none. The topology floor (0.05) and metric floor (0.001) act on the covariance eigenvalues; this acts on the log-log regression. Neither is touched and neither subsumes the other.

shrinkage_proposal.implemented: gp_bias_fix.shrunk_local_covariances (Ledoit-Wolf 2004 intensity, per point, target = global covariance rescaled to the point's own trace)
shrinkage_proposal.reason_1_wrong_size: its best possible effect is bounded above by the global_cov_broadcast row (D=1.6895 vs truth 2.0) -- it addresses the 10% term, and on its own still fails the gate: measured shrinkage+OLS on the square gives 1.6471, no better than plain OLS
shrinkage_proposal.reason_2_intensity_goes_the_wrong_way: the hypothesis predicted high intensity on isotropic data and mild on anisotropic. MEASURED: median alpha = 0.176 on the isotropic square and 1.000 on the 100:1 and 1000:1 anisotropic clouds. Ledoit-Wolf's denominator is ||Sigma_i - T||_F^2, and on a globally affine cloud the local covariance is already nearly proportional to the global one, so the target looks perfect and alpha saturates at 1. Adopting it would silently convert the distance arm into the GLOBAL arm on exactly the refutation family the local arm exists for -- the outcome the owner rejected.
shrinkage_proposal.composability: shrinkage+WLS was also measured (square 1.9228, cube 2.9521, 100:1 1.9494) and is neither needed nor harmful; it is left available but off.
